Players

Every profiled player in the selected mode — click a name to open their profile, or any header to sort. The # column is their standing in this mode.

How the standing is earned

On each hero, a player's result is the share of the other tracked players on that hero they finish above: 7th of 36 beats 29 of the other 35. The standing averages that share across their heroes, trusting a hero more when there are more players to beat on it (up to six) and when the player has more games on it.

That average is then pulled toward the middle of the board by how much evidence backs it, so a broad, well-played record leads when two records are close — and a thin record is only ever held back from the top, never pushed below a worse one.

Avg finish is the same share as a plain average, printed as where they usually place: Top 11% is ahead of 89% of each hero's players, 1st is first on every hero. The standing is an exact place: an exact tie breaks on Avg finish. A — instead of a place means too little evidence to rank yet, not a low rank.

Teammates

Who plays with whom, how often, and how it goes.

How to read this page

Together means on the same team in the same game, in Quick Match or Competitive. A group's games count every game its players shared a team, so a trio's games count toward each duo inside it too.

Dates count on the group's own clock — a day starts at the group's quietest hour, early morning Eastern — and the last 30 days run back from the newest game together on file (Nov 20, 2026), not from today.

Every section's own How to read link explains its numbers.

Squad record book

The group's records. A streak is one group's own games together, in order; a day runs from the group's quietest hour.

How these records work

Win streak together and Losing streak together are one group's games together in time order: games one of them played without the others do not break the run, and the QM/Comp line counts the run's own games. They replaced a squad-wide streak that ran over everyone's games at once — with this many of us in parallel lobbies, its longest run was a handful of people each playing solo, and as long as chance alone makes one.

Best day, Busiest day and the Best 7-day stretch count every match with a tracked player once, whoever played (156,372 stored matches; a floor of the true total). A day runs from the group's quietest hour, early morning Eastern, not from midnight, so a late session counts toward its evening. Under those cards the QM/Comp line splits that same window by mode and adds back to it. "Best" day/stretch are ranked by win rate (shrunk toward 50% for small samples), not raw win count — a losing record can never win either slot; the W–L shown is always the real, unshrunk record.

Every group

Games and win rate per mode, and Lift: how a group did against what its players win apart. No Lift here beats chance.

How to read these tables

Switch Duos / Trios / Quads / 5-stacks / 6-stacks above the table. Games and win rate together per mode, and Lift — the group's actual win rate minus the rate expected from the members' records outside the group (in points, ± its own error; descriptive, not causal: stacks also choose when and against whom they queue). No Lift here beats chance: none of the 1,321 survives a 5% false-discovery test across its own table, so none takes a colour — read the column as what these games did, not as chemistry. Click a group's row (▸) to drill in: Hero combos (each member's hero that match, one column per player) or Maps — click a member's name to go straight to their profile instead. Hover or tap a Lift for its 95% range.

Last played is the day a group last played together (the group's day runs from its quietest hour, as the record book's does). Last 30 days keeps the groups that played together in the 30 days before the newest game together on file (Nov 20, 2026), counted on the data's own clock rather than today's.

Groups need 5+ shared games to appear, and a mode shows — until it has 5 games of its own; Lift needs 10+ (a stricter floor — a 5-game sample is too thin for its own shrink to fully tame). The small number beside a rate is its games in that mode. Printed rates and sorting use the raw rate; hover a rate for its sample-shrunk twin (short lucky runs discounted), and * marks modes under 20 games.

Each Lift's ± is one standard error, and it counts the noise in what the members win apart as well as the group's own. A Lift takes a colour only when it survives a 5% false-discovery test across its own stack size's table — the test the hero pages use — so a grey one, however large, is inside what chance alone produces over that many rows.

Sizes overlap in these tables (unlike the Stacking cards below them, where each team counts once at its exact size — so a match where tracked players faced each other reads once for each side): a group's games count every match those players shared a team, so a 6-stack's games also appear in every duo, trio, quad and 5-stack inside it.

The Hero pairings table further down has its own Lift column: same idea, different comparison — a hero PAIR against what the two heroes' other duo line-ups add up to, not a player group against the average of its members' records apart.

In the drilldown, hero line-ups that occurred only once roll up into a one-off tally below the table.

Stacking

How often the group queues together, and whether stacks win more than the same players do alone.

How these are counted

How the group queues counts each team in each game once, by how many of our players were on it — a game where our players faced each other counts once for each side.

Does stacking help? reads each stacked team against the same players' solo games in the same mode: the team's result minus the average of its players' solo win rates (each shrunk toward 50% by 10 games; a team with a player under 20 solo games in that mode is left out). Its ± counts the noise in those solo rates as well as the stack's own, and a size takes a colour only past the bar a family of that many sizes needs.

Hero pairings

The partner heroes two of our players fielded beside each hero (10+ games); none of the 1,110 pairings beats chance.

How to read this section

The cards are the 8 heroes with the most line-ups: the three partner heroes each was fielded beside most, with their games and win rate together, and the table's Highest win % pick. All 57 heroes opens the full table.

The squad's line-ups from each hero's side — click a hero (▸) for every partner hero two tracked players fielded with it (10+-game pairings; a pairing appears under both its heroes). Line-ups counts one pair of players on one team in one match, so a trio's game counts once for each pair in it. Highest win % is picked by the sample-shrunk rate (raw % printed) — what won most here, not a pairing to pick; in the drilldown, the top duo's first name is the one playing this hero. Descriptive, not causal — who queues together also picks when and against whom. In the drilldown, Lift weighs each pairing against what its two heroes add up to in their other duo line-ups, and none of its 1,110 pairings beats chance across the section.

How to read this section

The chart draws the 6 heroes the squad wins least against and the 6 it wins most against, each from the squad's average; vs avg is the difference of the two printed rates, and All 57 heroes opens the full table.

The squad's record when the enemy team fields a hero (each enemy at their primary hero that match), QM + Competitive, over 1,205,782 hero-encounters. Baseline: the squad wins 49.8% of these; the 57 heroes span 14.4pp, from Ultron 43.7% 13,300g up to Black Widow 58.1% 9,847g. Per player these gaps are luck — only 1 of 5,325 gaps survives a 5% false-discovery correction, which is why player pages don't show them — but this spread is far too large and too deep to be chance.

Two caveats that the size of the numbers does not remove. Counting grain: a lobby is folded once per tracked player in it, so a stacked match counts several times — the counts are inflated and the rows are correlated (the rates are unaffected in expectation). Descriptive, not causal: who the enemy picks tracks map, mode and rank band, so a low row says the squad tends to lose lobbies that hero shows up in — not that the hero counters them. Rows under 100 encounters are omitted; hover a Win % for its sample-shrunk rate. Click a hero to open its page.
